Ludicrous

LOO-dih-krus -- shares a root with a Latin word for play or game. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Ludicrous is so foolish, unreasonable, or out of place as to be laughable.

The idea of building a ski resort in the middle of the desert struck everyone as ludicrous.

Worked Example

Someone proposes hosting an ice-skating competition on a beach in the middle of summer, and everyone in the room bursts out laughing at how impossible it sounds.

That absurd, laughably unreasonable quality is exactly what ludicrous describes. Unlike 'unlikely,' which just means improbable, ludicrous means so foolish it invites laughter.

How Ludicrous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

ridiculous

ridiculous: deserving or inviting mockery

absurd

absurd: wildly unreasonable or illogical

preposterous

preposterous: absurd or ridiculous to the point of being outrageous

Antonyms

sensible

sensible: having or showing good judgment

reasonable

reasonable: fair and sensible

How Strong Is It? — ridiculous → ludicrous → preposterous

ridiculous vs. ludicrous

ridiculous vs. ludicrous: Ridiculous is a more everyday word than ludicrous -- ridiculous can describe anything mildly silly, while ludicrous often implies the idea is so unreasonable it's genuinely laughable.

preposterous vs. ludicrous

preposterous vs. ludicrous: Preposterous can feel even stronger than ludicrous: ludicrous emphasizes something laughably foolish, while preposterous adds a sense of shock that anyone could seriously propose it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Ludicrous comes from Latin ludicrus, 'playful, like a game,' from ludus, 'play' -- the same root behind interlude. Calling an idea ludicrous treats something seriously proposed as if it were merely a game or a joke.

Use the root in a new word: interlude

Use the root in a new word: interlude: The orchestra played a short musical interlude between the play's two main acts.

Word Choice

Ludicrous is often used to dismiss an idea, claim, or plan as too absurd to take seriously, as in 'a ludicrous suggestion.'
